key_insight: Diffusion language models need to know when regeneration will actually help—not just which tokens look uncertain. Sudoku experiments suggest that hidden states reveal errors missed by token confidence, while revising an isolated error often repeats it if the surrounding context stays fixed.
problem_solved: Remasking lets diffusion language models revise generated text, but token confidence can be an unreliable guide, and unchanged surrounding context can prevent successful correction.
method: Diagnose error detection and remasking behavior on Sudoku tasks.
Examine error signals in hidden states and test whether isolated remasking corrects mistakes.
Introduce DiVR, a verifier that predicts whether a partially generated sequence will reach a correct answer; the provided abstract ends before its training details.
impact: The findings point practitioners toward hidden-state verification rather than token confidence alone when designing regeneration policies. They also highlight the need to consider surrounding context when attempting corrections.

paper_title: Learning When Diffusion Language Models Should Regenerate
paper_authors: Minhae Oh, Jeonghye Kim, Jinwoo Koo, Yeongoon Kim, Jimin Seo
